stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta to Add Voice Agents, Completing a $3.6B+ CX Stack Build-Out
stories.body: Salesforce agreed to acquire Cresta — whose voice agents handle complex customer calls for brands including Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines — with the deal expected to close in Q1 FY28 (Feb–Apr 2027). This follows Salesforce's September 2026 close of its $3.6B acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom), positioning Fin as fast-to-deploy for mid-market and Cresta for high-volume enterprise voice. Cresta also launched end-to-end self-service developer tooling on October 29, 2026, letting enterprise teams build, test, and deploy production agents in as little as one week without vendor assistance.
stories.why: Two named competitors — Cresta and Intercom Fin — are now inside Salesforce's Service Cloud, which changes the competitive landscape for every enterprise CX deal; sellers need to know what Salesforce now owns versus what remains independent, and how Cresta's 'Deputy Agent' cross-system persistence compares to what Graas delivers. The self-serve build pathway also feeds the build-vs-buy conversation directly.

stories.title: Neo4j Launches Context Engine — a Six-Layer Business Ontology and Graph-Native Memory for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced the Context Engine, a new product that lets enterprises rapidly build a shared knowledge layer — a reusable, governed substrate of business ontology, data connections, and agent memory — so AI agents can reason consistently over enterprise data. The product includes a predefined six-layer graph model mapping an organization's structure, processes, data, and AI assets, plus a graph-native memory layer that logs agent reasoning and decision paths as a permanent record. It also ships MCP server configuration tooling, connecting physical data sources to business logic for context-aware agent decisions at runtime.
stories.why: This is the most direct recent proof that the 'context layer before agents' architecture argument has gone mainstream — a major graph vendor shipping it as a named product on October 20 gives sellers a concrete, dateable milestone to anchor the conversation. It also validates Graas's framing that raw CRM or ERP data is insufficient context for reliable retail agents.

stories.title: McKinsey 'State of AI 2026': 32% of Enterprises Cancelled a Software Buy to Build with Agents, Yet Enterprise EBIT Impact Stays Flat at 37%
stories.body: McKinsey's 'The State of AI in 2026: On the Road to ROI,' based on 1,719 respondents across 97 countries surveyed May–June 2026, found that 32% of organizations decided against buying at least one software product or feature because they could build it in-house with agentic coding tools. Among enterprises over $1B in revenue, 40% are now scaling agents in one or more functions, up from 27% the prior year. Despite these gains, the share of organizations reporting enterprise-level EBIT impact stayed flat at 37% year-over-year, and about one in five organizations report AI operating costs are already constraining their AI use.
stories.why: The 32% build-vs-buy statistic is a live objection on every enterprise sales call — sellers need the rebuttal that building eliminates the vendor but not the run cost, governance debt, or context infrastructure required for agents to work. The flat EBIT number is equally powerful: it explains why pilots stall and why a purpose-built retail context layer accelerates the path from productivity to profit.

stories.title: BCG and McKinsey Both Publish October 2026 Research Showing CPG Agentic AI at Commercial Inflection — but 59% of CPG Firms Have No Meaningful Capabilities Yet
stories.body: BCG's October 2026 GenAI CPG Survey found that while CPG companies piloting owned AI agents are seeing 3–10% revenue growth, 59% of CPG companies report no meaningful agentic AI capabilities today, and only 4% of consumers will allow an AI agent to complete a purchase autonomously. BCG's separate supply chain research found agentic AI can boost in-stocks by 2–4% and planning productivity by over 60% for CPGs and retailers. McKinsey's October 9, 2026 CPG article separately showed that AI performance management agents can cut commercial team effort in half by tracking KPIs, detecting variances, and recommending actions — but stressed that agents need synthesized data across retailer performance, promotional results, inventory, and digital-shelf metrics to function overnight.
stories.why: The 59% capability gap is a direct addressable market signal for Graas: the majority of large CPG companies know they need agents but haven't built the data foundation to run them. The BCG in-stock and McKinsey effort-reduction figures give sellers outcome-anchored proof points to use in supply chain and commercial planning conversations.

stories.title: Decagon Launches Voice 3, Personal Agent Gateway, and Joins OpenAI's B2B Marketplace at $4.5B Valuation
stories.body: In October 2026, Decagon — valued at $4.5B — launched Voice 3 (featuring its first proprietary speech model, Chord), a Personal Agent Gateway, and became a launch partner on OpenAI's new B2B marketplace, where eligible OpenAI enterprise customers can apply existing OpenAI spend toward Decagon. The company simultaneously expanded its stated scope beyond ticket resolution, saying its agents now qualify leads, onboard customers, collect payments, and grow relationships. Sierra, the market leader at a $15.8B valuation and over $200M in annualized revenue, launched its own Compliance Console on October 28, 2026 — configurable guardrails for multi-channel, multi-jurisdiction agent outreach built into its Horizon platform.
stories.why: Decagon's pivot from 'support only' to a full customer revenue lifecycle agent — and its OpenAI marketplace distribution — means it is now competing closer to Graas's territory on onboarding and growth workflows, not just deflection. Sierra's Compliance Console signals that enterprise buyers are demanding governance controls as a table-stakes capability before signing agent contracts.
